sources.entry: imgproxy - Fast and secure standalone server for resizing and converting remote images. (Source Code) MIT Go/Docker/K8S

summary.one_liner: imgproxy is a standalone HTTP server that resizes, processes, and converts remote images on the fly via specially crafted URLs.
summary.what_it_does: It fetches a source image from a URL, applies processing options encoded in the request URL (resizing, cropping, rotating, watermarking, filters), and serves the result. Output can be used directly in HTML, CSS, or JavaScript as an ordinary image URL. It supports format conversion (basic formats include JPEG, PNG, GIF, WebP, AVIF, and JPEG XL), color profile and metadata stripping, PNG quantization, and simple smart cropping. Security options include signed image URLs, checking image type and real dimensions before full decoding, HTTP header authorization, and restrictions on image sources, file size, and processing options. The README says it is built on libvips.
use_cases: resize images on the fly for a web app
serve image thumbnails from remote URLs
convert images to WebP or AVIF
offload image processing from an application server
strip metadata and optimize images for delivery
generate signed image URLs to prevent abuse
notable: Drop-in replacement for in-app image processing code, processing images on demand
Built on libvips with a low memory footprint, per the README
Image bomb protection by checking real dimensions before decoding
Signed URLs and HTTP header authorization to restrict access
Paid imgproxy Pro edition adds video, PDF, and Photoshop previews, plus advanced features
caveats: Advanced features such as video/PDF/Photoshop previews, object detection, and SSIM-based auto-quality are only in the paid imgproxy Pro edition
HTTPS is not built in; the README expects it to be handled by a CDN, load balancer, or reverse proxy
